hints: The requested game counts are degrees of a simple graph.
A player with highest remaining degree can be connected to players with the next highest degrees.
Repeat this Havel-Hakimi reduction using a max-heap.
analogy: Give the busiest player games against the other busiest available players, then update their remaining requests.
example: Degrees [2,1,1] yield games 1-2 and 1-3; degrees [2,0,0] are impossible.
algorithm: Store positive remaining degrees with player IDs in a max-heap. Remove the largest d, then remove d other players with largest positive degrees, create a game with each, decrement them, and reinsert positive remainders. If fewer than d players are available print IMPOSSIBLE; otherwise output all games.
correctness: The Havel-Hakimi theorem says this reduction preserves whether a degree sequence is realizable. Each step fixes all remaining games of one player with distinct other players, so a completed construction has exactly the requested degrees.
complexity: For n players and total requested degree S, O((n+S) log n) time and O(n+S) space.
